dialect.guess: Micro Focus COBOL (likely MF Personal COBOL or MF COBOL for DOS/Windows)
evidence: $set LINKCOUNT"448" compiler directive at top (Micro Focus style)
CRT STATUS IS KEY-STATUS (Micro Focus screen handling)
CURSOR IS CSTART, CONSOLE IS CRT (Micro Focus special-names)
X"B3", X"CD" hex literals for box-drawing characters (PC/DOS era)
COPY statements with .SL, .FDE, .FD, .WS, .ID suffixes (Micro Focus library conventions)

purpose.summary: POSTCHQ posts cheques from a batch/print file to the accounts payable system. It handles both normal cheques and post-dated cheques (routing the latter to a PDCHEQ file), updates creditor accounts, and generates a printed audit report with batch and page numbering.

notable_features: COMP-3 (packed decimal) for monetary and batch fields
CRT STATUS / CURSOR / CONSOLE special-names for interactive terminal support
Extensive use of COPY statements for file definitions and working-storage
Box-drawing characters (X"B3", X"CD", "³", "°") for screen UI
Post-dated cheque handling via PDCHEQ file
Printer control fields with condensed/expanded print type codes
GNU GPL copyright notice embedded in SECURITY paragraph
181 PERFORM statements and 115 GOTO statements indicating complex procedural flow
verdict.notes: Source is truncated to first 16000 characters; the PROCEDURE DIVISION is not visible in the excerpt but the structural indicators confirm 2371 code lines and 181 PERFORMs/115 GOTOs. The program is clearly a real-world accounts payable cheque posting system authored by J.W. Lemmon (APAC), version 8.13.07 dated March 2008, licensed under GPL v2+. The use of PC box-drawing characters and Micro Focus-specific features strongly suggests a DOS/Windows Micro Focus COBOL environment.
